subject: Clymber POC — evaluation gating & ops handshake
body:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@clymber.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Clymber POC — evaluation gating & ops handshake

Hi Sara — great to connect today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we can get the POC running next week.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary use case: customer support triage + automated response suggestion on multi-turn threads.
- Target model behavior: low hallucination on factual replies, high intent extraction precision for routing.
- Expected average input length: ~350 tokens; occasional up to 1,200 tokens.
- Traffic profile: bursty; average 25 qps, peak 80 qps during morning batch windows.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
1) Integration: Redwood-hosted inference endpoint + SDK integration for evaluation.
2) Acceptance checks: telemetry-driven KPIs (see below).
3) Onboarding: sample workload ingestion + test harness run by Redwood.

Initial acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: P50 <= 120 ms, P95 <= 350 ms for 512-token requests (measured at customer's egress).
- Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent active requests with <= 400 ms median latency under realistic batching.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0008 during evaluation window (we'll report tokens consumed).
- Quality: automated intent extraction precision >= 92% on your labeled set; human preference rate >= 75% over baseline responses on a 500-sample blind eval.
- Stability: no more than 2 infra-related errors/hour during steady-state runs.

Data & artifacts we need from you to start:
- 5k representative user prompts (anonymized) by Tue 19 Jan.
- Example conversation threads (10 long-form examples).
- Expected success cases and a short rubric (1-pager).

Next steps / owners:
- Mateo (me): finalize commercial/POC scope and set kickoff.
- Ben (SE): technical onboarding and test harness.
- Lauren (CS): success criteria owner & evaluation coordination.
- Sara / Clymber: provide workload samples and any compliance constraints.

Attachments: clymber_poc_onepager.xlsx (POC plan), redwood_onboarding_checklist.pdf (onboarding tasks).

If that reads OK, I propose kickoff on Tue 20 Jan and a quick smoke run the week of 20–22 Jan.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@clymber.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clymber POC — evaluation gating & ops handshake

Thanks, Mateo — that looks clear and very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from our side:
1) Data: we can provide 5k anonymized prompts by EOD Mon 19 Jan. We'll include labels for intent for ~2k of those.
2) Model footprint: do you support a private/dedicated instance if we need to avoid shared tenancy during the POC?
3) Cost metric: can you confirm whether cost/token is estimated before or after tokenization and whether you include embeddings calls in the token count?

We are keen to keep the POC to a tight 2-week window but want to ensure we agree on measurement methods. Happy to kick off Tue 20 if you can start the endpoint earlier.

Best,
Sara Jensen
Head of Product, Clymber Labs
Sara.Jensen@clymber.com

Thanks for the quick reply, Sara. Short answers: yes, we can provision a dedicated instance for the POC (Dedicated mode) if required — we'll treat that as an add-on for a timeboxed window.

On cost/token — we report cost after tokenization (model tokens consumed). For hybrid flows that also call out to embedding endpoints we'll report embeddings token usage separately; the POC cost target I proposed above excludes embedding units unless we use them for reranking. We'll label all cost components in the final report.

Ben will own the technical onboarding. Ben — can you confirm the smoke-test harness and the expected length of time to get a dedicated endpoint provisioned? Also attaching a sample load profile for the kind of burstiness Sara mentioned.

Mateo

Hi all — looping in with the technical acceptance checklist and measurement approach. Attaching load_profile_sample.json.

Technical acceptance checklist (details):
- Test harness: we'll run a 12-hour steady-state run + 3 x synthetic burst tests (5 min, 30s ramp, peak load) using your anonymized prompts.
- Latency measurement: device-level (customer egress) p50/p95/p99; we'll report both cold and warm cache figures. For fairness, we recommend excluding outliers due to network issues (above 5s).
- Throughput: validation that 50 concurrent sessions maintain baseline latency (median <= 400 ms). We'll include CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rate in the report.
- Cost accounting: we will produce a per-request token breakdown (prompt/response) and an aggregated cost/token for the run window.
- Quality validation: we'll run a blind A/B on 500 labeled samples you provide (A = your baseline, B = Redwood output) and report preference rate. We'll also run an automated NER/intent extraction script against the labeled set to compute precision/recall.

Provisioning / timeline notes:
- Dedicated endpoint provision: ~48 hours from signed SOW. If you prefer hosted endpoint for initial smoke we can stand that up in < 4 hours.
- SE onboarding + test harness setup: 1 business day after we receive sample prompts and a small API key.

Attachments: load_profile_sample.json (sample traffic pattern).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0166

Hi team — thanks for the clear plan. I own the evaluation cadence from Redwood's side and will be the primary contact for results and success measurement. A few quick alignment points so there is zero ambiguity on owners and timing: 

- Kickoff: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 — 30-min sync to confirm sample placement and endpoint details. Mateo to schedule.
- Customer deliverables: Clymber to provide 5k anonymized prompts and 500 labeled eval samples by Mon, 19 Jan EOD (Sara).
- Redwood deliverables: stand up hosted endpoint for smoke by Tue 20 Jan (Ben). If you need a dedicated instance, sign SOW and allow 48 hours for provisioning.
- Measurement windows: smoke run (20 Jan), steady-state window (21–22 Jan), final report by Fri 23 Jan.
- Final acceptance: we will summarize the KPI report and run a 1-hr review call. If targets above are met we will recommend next steps (options: extend to dedicated or scale to production).

I'll kick off the calendar invites once Mateo confirms the kickoff time. Looking forward to this — we'll keep the POC tight and data-driven.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
